claim: The Phase H decision push-back drain (src/runtime/decision_push.py + scripts/ops/push_decisions_back.py) has been unable to distinguish 'its work-object store was archived by the 2026-09-21 reset' from 'there is genuinely nothing to push' since 2026-09-21, because push_decisions_back.py::_iter_objects() returns an empty list on a missing OBJECTS_DIR exactly as it would on an empty one.
evidence: ls docs/claude/work/objects -> 'No such file or directory' (the directory named in CLAUDE.md's retirement note: 'Retired 2026-09-21 ... the work store (docs/claude/work/objects|intents|steps/) ... Do not resurrect them'). python3 scripts/ops/push_decisions_back.py --queue > /tmp/out2.txt 2>&1; echo $? -> real exit 0, stdout 'push_decisions_back — queue depth 0' with deliver/skip_* all 0 and 'Nothing to push. Record the empty run with --receipt so nothing to do stays distinguishable from the drain died' -- no mention the directory itself is gone. Source: scripts/ops/push_decisions_back.py lines 90/108-113 (`OBJECTS_DIR = REPO/docs/claude/work/objects`; `_iter_objects(): if not OBJECTS_DIR.exists(): return out` before the glob). Contrast, same run: python3 scripts/ci/check_decision_answers.py > /tmp/out1.txt 2>&1; echo $? -> real exit 1, stderr 'docs/claude/work/objects is not a directory' (verified with output redirected to a file and $? read directly, after an earlier piped-through-`tail` check wrongly suggested exit 0 -- caught and corrected before filing). scripts/ops/render_due_list.py's src_spent_decision_edges also checks `.is_dir()` first and returns 'not_applicable' with a clear note. Only the push-back drain's own reader lacks this guard. src/runtime/decision_push.py::render_push_message (line ~246) still hard-codes 'Truth of record: docs/claude/work/objects/{object_id}.yaml' in the text pushed to a woken session.
expected: A drain whose data source was deleted six days ago reports 'could not look' (or refuses to run), the same way scripts/ci/check_decision_answers.py and render_due_list.py's spent-decision-edges source already do for the identical directory.
actual: The drain silently reports a healthy empty queue ('queue depth 0'), identical to what it would report if the store existed and genuinely had nothing pending; its companion module still names the retired path in operator-facing push text.
population: n=1 subsystem (Phase H decision push-back: work_decisions.py / decision_push.py / push_decisions_back.py / blocked_lane_watch.py / commit_work_decisions.py). The objects directory itself: 0 files (does not exist). Not measured: whether any workflow or session has attempted to write a decision_requests[] block since 2026-09-21 -- if none has, today's practical blast radius is 'orphaned silently' rather than 'actively dropping a delivered decision', but that is inferred, not measured.
detector: None today for push_decisions_back.py's reader specifically. scripts/ci/check_decision_answers.py already proves the correct behavior is achievable (it fails loud on the same missing directory) and could be extended, or its is_dir() check could be factored out and reused by _iter_objects().
proposed_fix: In scripts/ops/push_decisions_back.py::_iter_objects(), replace the silent `if not OBJECTS_DIR.exists(): return out` with a raised/reported 'could not look' state distinct from an empty list, mirroring check_decision_answers.py's main() guard; update decision_push.py::render_push_message to stop naming docs/claude/work/objects/ or to name wherever decision_requests now lives.

claim: src/runtime/operator_owed.py::grade_item collapses 'we could not measure whether a genuinely-human item moved' (carries_unchanged=None) into STATE_MOVED -- the exact collapsed-state failure the module's own docstring says it exists to prevent -- for any genuinely_human-owner item whose age is inside its budget.
evidence: Reproduced directly: `python3 -c "import datetime as dt; from src.runtime.operator_owed import grade_item; now=dt.datetime(2026,9,27,tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc); item={'id':'OI-TEST-1','owner_class':'judgement','severity':'medium','last_state_change_at':'2026-09-20T00:00:00+00:00'}; g=grade_item(item, carries_unchanged=None, now=now); print(g['state'], g['reason'])"` -> prints `moved owner_class='judgement' needs a person; graded on AGE only (7.00d of a 7.00d budget). Carry is not applied -- no session can move this item, so counting sessions would only manufacture a mute button.` -- the printed reason explicitly says carry does not apply and nothing counts as a move, yet the returned state is 'moved'. Root cause: operator_owed.py line 319, `out['state'] = STATE_CARRIED if carries_unchanged else STATE_MOVED` treats carries_unchanged=None and carries_unchanged=0 identically (both falsy), where the module's own docstring for the STATES section says 'None means the caller could not measure it -- which is not_measurable, never zero. A zero is a real reading.' tests/test_operator_owed.py exercises genuinely-human items only with carries_unchanged=99 (test_carry_does_not_apply_to_a_genuinely_human_item) or with an unreadable date (test_a_genuinely_human_item_with_no_readable_date_is_not_graded_clean, which takes a different early-return branch) -- no test passes a genuinely-human item with a READABLE in-budget age AND carries_unchanged=None, so the gap has no covering test. SEPARATELY: `git grep -n grade_item -- '*.py'` shows grade_item is called only from tests/test_operator_owed.py; the two production importers of src.runtime.operator_owed (scripts/ops/render_due_list.py, scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py) import only OPEN_STATUSES/TERMINAL_STATUSES, never grade_item -- so this is currently dead code in production despite the docstring presenting it as the canonical grader for the operator-owed register.
expected: carries_unchanged=None on a genuinely-human item with in-budget age returns STATE_NOT_MEASURABLE (matching the module's own stated rule that None is never treated as zero), or grade_item is wired into the one production script (scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py) that actually computes operator-owed escalation, which today reimplements its own separate, non-drift-checked age/carry logic instead of importing this module.
actual: Returns STATE_MOVED with a self-contradicting reason string; grade_item has zero production callers today, so the bug is latent rather than live.
population: n=1 function, reproduced with 1 synthetic item; no test in tests/test_operator_owed.py covers the (genuinely_human, age in-budget, carries_unchanged=None) cell of the state table.
detector: tests/test_operator_owed.py exists and is thorough elsewhere but has no test for this specific cell; adding one would catch a regression once (if ever) grade_item gets a production caller.
proposed_fix: Change line 319 to explicitly branch on `carries_unchanged is None` (-> STATE_NOT_MEASURABLE) vs `== 0` (-> STATE_MOVED) vs positive (-> STATE_CARRIED), and add the missing test cell; separately, decide whether grade_item should be wired into scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py or documented as superseded/retired so the docstring stops presenting dead code as canonical.

claim: src/runtime/alert_cooldown.py::cooldown_admits, on an unreadable per-kind cooldown-state file, does not merely alert for the key it was called with (the documented, intended behaviour) -- it also silently overwrites the whole shared state file, discarding every OTHER key's live cooldown latch for that alert kind.
evidence: Reproduced: wrote a state file with two live latches {'keyA': t0, 'keyB': t0}, corrupted it to invalid JSON (simulating a transient unreadable-file condition), then called `cooldown_admits('test', 'keyC', cooldown_s=3600, path_resolver=lambda k: path)`. Logged 'test cooldown state unreadable (...) - alerting rather than suppressing' and returned True (correct, documented behaviour for keyC). But the file on disk afterward was `{"keyC": <now>}` -- keyA and keyB's timestamps are gone. Root cause: alert_cooldown.py's load_state() returns ({}, False) on any read failure, and cooldown_admits() only branches on `readable` to skip the SUPPRESS check (correct) -- it does not skip the unconditional prune-and-save at the bottom (lines 186-192), which persists `state` (== {} when unreadable) plus the new key, replacing the file.
expected: An unreadable-but-still-present state file either (a) is left untouched on disk when it cannot be safely parsed, so other keys' latches survive a transient glitch, or (b) the overwrite-on-unreadable behaviour is a stated, deliberate part of the 'alert rather than suppress' design (in which case the module docstring should say so, since today it only argues for alerting on the current key, not for discarding every sibling key's state).
actual: Any single unreadable-file event for a shared alert kind (e.g. target_naked_alert_state.json, which the module docstring says covers every symbol/account combination with an active condition) silently resets every other key's cooldown for that kind, which could cause a burst of already-cooling-down alerts to look freshly eligible right after a transient disk hiccup.
population: n=1 reproduction against a synthetic file; not measured against the live trader's actual runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json files or how often a genuine (non-benign) read failure has occurred there -- save_state uses tempfile+os.replace so an ordinary concurrent write should not itself corrupt the file; the realistic trigger is closer to disk-level corruption or truncation than a race.
detector: None today. tests/ for alert_cooldown were not located/enumerated in this pass (out of the read-in-full set); if a test module exists it was not checked for this specific case.
proposed_fix: In cooldown_admits(), when readable is False, still write the new key's timestamp but merge it into a freshly-read-if-possible-else-untouched file rather than replacing the whole file with just the one key -- or, at minimum, log that other keys' state may have been discarded so the loss is visible rather than silent.

claim: The dashboard/diag 'stopped' heartbeat label (src/runtime/heartbeat.py) fires 3x sooner than the actual watchdog restart-eligible alarm threshold (scripts/check_heartbeat.py), a mismatch the module's own docstring already discloses as unreconciled rather than hides.
evidence: src/runtime/heartbeat.py heartbeat_thresholds(): cadence defaults to HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60s; 'stopped' at age >= cadence*10 = 600s (10 minutes). scripts/check_heartbeat.py: `threshold = tick_interval_s * grace_factor` with argparse defaults TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS=900, HEARTBEAT_GRACE_FACTOR=2.0 -> threshold=1800s (30 minutes) before the watchdog even considers auto-restart. heartbeat.py's own module comment already states: 'scripts/check_heartbeat.py still uses TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS x HEARTBEAT_GRACE_FACTOR for its alarm threshold; that is a separate watchdog and is left at its current convention pending a follow-up alignment.'
expected: N/A -- this is a disclosed, not hidden, inconsistency; flagged for completeness since it means an operator can see 'stopped' on the dashboard for up to 20 minutes before the automated watchdog treats the same condition as alarm-worthy.
actual: Confirmed the disclosed gap is still live and unreconciled as of 2026-09-27; not a new finding, just a still-open one worth a due-date since it has no tracking row found in this pass.
population: n=2 modules compared, default env values only (both are env-overridable; a deployment-specific override was not checked against the live VM in this pass).
detector: None; this is a convention mismatch, not a bug either module would catch in itself.
proposed_fix: Either align the dashboard 'stopped' threshold with the watchdog's actual restart-eligible threshold, or document on the dashboard/diag surface itself that 'stopped' means 'display threshold', not 'the watchdog is about to act'.
